findings.summary: The call in progress is forgotten only when it succeeds, so after a call raises every later call with that key awaits the same failed task and gets the old exception forever.
A call that joins a call in progress is counted as a miss, not a hit, so cache_info() reports one miss per caller.

Calls in progress are grouped by the id of the cache accessor, which every instance shares, and methodkey leaves out self, so a concurrent call on one instance gets another instance's result (one user's data served to another).
update_wrapper runs after the cache attributes are set, so it copies the wrapped function's __dict__ over them and a stacked decorator reports the inner decorator's cache, cache_key and cache_clear.
cache_clear() also empties the table of calls in progress, so a call that is running when the cache is cleared fails with KeyError (when _run deletes its entry) for every caller waiting on it.
